messages.Assuming no temperature change performe: Assuming no temperature change performed equally well or better, so the rating is not green.

messages.-hour forecasts in this period yet. New: -hour forecasts in this period yet. New forecasts start being recorded after updating; previous short-term predictions cannot be converted into these comparisons.
messages.A door/window contact sensor can monitor: A door/window contact sensor can monitor the fireplace damper position. Select the sensor state that means the fireplace is in use. For a damper contact sensor, Open normally means active and Closed means inactive. Door/window labels are converted to Home Assistant’s underlying on/off values. Other sensors show their declared options, current valid state and any saved value. A contact state indicates the damper position; it does not prove that a fire is burning.
messages.Active/Passive season setpoints can chan: Active/Passive season setpoints can change real thermostats. Heating schedules remain simulated.
Actual heating can differ from the plan. This is not a live-control readiness guarantee.
messages.Add the configured rooms affected by thi: Add the configured rooms affected by this heat source. Select each room once. Rooms already assigned to another zone must first be removed from that zone. Main room choices are limited to the rooms added here. Zone membership does not replace a room’s primary thermostat or heating system. Garage rooms use their own controller and are not linked to shared zones.
messages.Air-to-air heat pump control changes HVA: Air-to-air heat pump control changes HVAC modes, fan modes and any selected swing mode. Simulation sends no heat pump commands. Enable live control?
messages.All room timelines share the price chart: All room timelines share the price chart’s time axis.

messages.Allows ThermalPilot to control the selec: Allows ThermalPilot to control the selected zone heat pump for the selected use when global live control is enabled. Off observes the pump without controlling it. If ThermalPilot was already controlling it, it first returns the pump to fan-only standby.
messages.Allows real thermostat setpoint changes: Allows real thermostat setpoint changes when ThermalPilot changes between Active and Passive. Active applies each room’s target temperature; Passive applies the seasonal fallback: the shared summer setpoint or each room’s normal target in winter. These commands can occur even with simulation enabled. This does not enable live heating schedule control.
messages.Approximate comparison for room cooling-: Approximate comparison for room cooling-speed badges and a starting prior for new room models. Learned values are never overwritten and this selection does not reset learning. References are older whole-building examples, not insulation grades. Unknown keeps the general cooling-speed bands. Garages use their own starting estimate and the general bands.
messages.Automatic heating starts when the garage: Automatic heating starts when the garage sensor drops below this limit. Outdoors above this value turns the pump off; at or below it, idle operation uses fan-only.
messages.Average absolute difference of saved 3-h: Average absolute difference of saved 3-hour forecasts from measurements over the last 7 days:
messages.Blue: predicted temperature under the pr: Blue: predicted temperature under the proposed plan. This outcome has not been observed.
messages.COMFORT PLANNING · observation and learn: COMFORT PLANNING · observation and learning, no thermostat control
messages.Changing heat distribution restarts room: Changing heat distribution restarts room-response learning because the heating input changes. Recorded history is retained. Continue?
messages.Choose a ThermalPilot integration in the: Choose a ThermalPilot integration in the card settings.
messages.Choose the interface language. Room and: Choose the interface language. Room and entity names remain unchanged. Save settings to keep the choice. Embedded history cards follow this choice where supported by Home Assistant.
messages.Choose the main room sensor, the average: Choose the main room sensor, the average of all linked sensors, or the coldest room. All linked sensors must be available. Heating pauses if any linked room reaches the shared upper limit.
messages.Choose your heating system and house det: Choose your heating system and house details. Heat distribution determines which sensor inputs are needed.
messages.Clear means the windows receive direct s: Clear means the windows receive direct sunlight without major obstructions. Choose Partly shaded for some trees, buildings or overhangs, or Mostly shaded when sunlight is usually blocked. Forecasts use a more cautious solar allowance: partly shaded uses 65% and mostly shaded 30% of the clear allowance. Actual room warming is still learned from observations; no solar heat is assumed before learning. Seasonal leaf cover and changing shading can still affect accuracy.
messages.Collected-data coverage, not model relia: Collected-data coverage, not model reliability. Least-observed room: {heating} heating hours and {idle} idle hours. Collection began {days} days ago. Limited: 3 hours each / 1 day; Developing: 12 hours each / 3 days; Good: 48 hours each / 14 days; High: 120 hours each / 42 days. All criteria must be met. Learning continues at every level.
messages.Comfort planning uses room temperature,: Comfort planning uses room temperature, outdoor temperature and observed heating demand. Electricity prices are not required; no heating schedules or thermostat commands are generated.
messages.Compare recorded temperatures with forec: Compare recorded temperatures with forecasts saved hours earlier. The accuracy cards also compare against predicting no temperature change. Forecasts assume the proposed heating plan; actual heating may differ, especially during simulation.
messages.Compare rooms under the same conditions:: Compare rooms under the same conditions:
messages.Construction of this garage only. It doe: Construction of this garage only. It does not inherit the house type or reset learning. Garage-specific construction benchmarks are not yet available, so all garage types keep the general cooling-speed bands and the four-hour starting estimate until observations teach the actual response.
messages.Cooling-speed bands are provisional: und: Cooling-speed bands are provisional: under 1 h, 1–2 h, 2–4 h, 4–8 h, and 8 h or longer per 1°C drop. For a selected house type, badges instead compare with that type: under 0.5×, 0.5–0.8×, 0.8–1.25×, 1.25–2×, and at least 2× its reference cooling time. Initial rooms share starting estimates and remain unrated. Comparisons become more useful as their heat-loss parameters adapt to observations. Wind, ventilation, sensor placement and unmeasured heat sources can affect the estimates. The listed time describes this reference test, not how long heating can safely remain off in your home.
messages.Current relay or thermostat demand; On d: Current relay or thermostat demand; On does not guarantee water flow.
messages.Degrees added to each room’s target temp: Degrees added to each room’s target temperature during a suggested heating window. For example, a 20 °C target with a 1.5 °C boost suggests a 21.5 °C thermostat setpoint to store heat. Scheduled targets remain simulated in this version.
messages.Device setpoint used in Heat mode. Exter: Device setpoint used in Heat mode. External room sensors and the heating plan decide when to switch between Heat and Fan only. This is separate from each room’s comfort target.
messages.Door contact sensors pause garage heatin: Door contact sensors pause garage heating when any selected door stays open longer than Pause heating after door opens. The pump switches to fan-only. One shared timer starts when the first selected door opens and keeps running while any selected door remains open. It resets when all selected doors are closed.
messages.Each row shows the latest observation wi: Each row shows the latest observation within its 15-minute interval, not an average. Suggested thermostat target is the setting ThermalPilot would apply, not a room-temperature forecast. Table shows up to 288 intervals. Original observations remain stored internally. Short chart views use 15-minute time labels; longer views use wider intervals.
messages.Electric heating benefits mainly from ch: Electric heating benefits mainly from changing electricity tariffs. Other heat sources use observation only: no schedules, no thermostat control and no required price sensor. Heat-pump efficiency and fuel costs are not modeled.
messages.Electricity prices from now and outdoor: Electricity prices from now and outdoor temperature
Electricity prices from now and outdoor temperature and heating water temperature are available. Weather forecast details are reported separately below.
Electricity prices from now and outdoor temperature are available. Weather forecast details are reported separately below.
messages.Embedded history is unavailable. Open th: Embedded history is unavailable. Open the full Home Assistant history below.
messages.Emergency lower temperature limit shared: Emergency lower temperature limit shared by all rooms. Each room’s own target is the normal comfort goal. ThermalPilot prioritizes avoiding this limit even when electricity is expensive; this value is not the idle thermostat target.
messages.Enable real thermostat control? If anoth: Enable real thermostat control? If another automation controls these thermostats, disable it first. ThermalPilot will apply its scheduled targets, even while the model is still learning. Missing essential data returns affected rooms to their seasonal fallback temperature.
messages.Forecasts are compared with measurements: Forecasts are compared with measurements within five minutes of their due time. “Similar heating” means observed demand matched the forecast for at least 90% of observations, with no large recording gaps. These counts give context, not a guarantee of accuracy.
messages.Garage temperature cycle: heat below the: Garage temperature cycle: heat below the lower limit; fan-only after the upper limit. Warm weather turns the pump off.
messages.Heat means heating mode; pauses use fan-: Heat means heating mode; pauses use fan-only. Room sensors govern temperature limits. The device setpoint is separate from those limits.
messages.Heat storage or a bridging run ahead of: Heat storage or a bridging run ahead of predicted cooling.
messages.Heating in winter / cooling in summer: Heating in winter / cooling in summer
messages.Heating only operates in winter. Cooling: Heating only operates in winter. Cooling only operates in summer. Both heats in winter and cools in summer. Automatic season changes must persist for 24 hours. Reversing between heating and cooling requires confirmed fan-only standby for ten minutes; automatic Heat/Cool mode is never used.
messages.Heating water temperature is not availab: Heating water temperature is not available; planning and learning use observed thermostat demand without water-temperature adjustment.
messages.History collection and learning paused b: History collection and learning paused because outdoor temperature is unavailable. Existing model parameters are retained.
messages.History entities are being registered. R: History entities are being registered. Refresh this page shortly.
messages.Hourly average uses fixed hourly average: Hourly average uses fixed hourly averages of the source prices. 15 minutes plans using quarter-hour intervals. Flexible builds heating sessions in 15-minute steps, allowing runs such as 60 or 75 minutes while respecting the minimum flexible heating run.
messages.House badges compare cooling speed with: House badges compare cooling speed with this approximate reference. Garage badges use the general bands.
messages.How heat reaches rooms: circulating wate: How heat reaches rooms: circulating water in floors or radiators, electric floor/ceiling/panels, or warm air. Mixed means different rooms use different systems. Water distribution can optionally use a heating-water sensor and uses valve timing. Electric and warm-air distribution ignore those inputs and learn response from observed thermostat demand. Mixed and Other retain water requirements until room overrides are supported.
messages.Initial collection is complete. Waiting: Initial collection is complete. Waiting for saved 3-hour forecasts that can be compared with actual measurements. Learning continues.
messages.Initial estimate of how slowly heat inpu: Initial estimate of how slowly heat input affects room temperature and how long its effect persists. Concrete slabs often need a longer delay, but lightweight floors, radiators, electric heaters and air systems also have a response time. Use a shorter value for faster systems. This remains relevant to every distribution; it is separate from valve opening or closing time.
messages.Initial model: needs at least 12 heating: Initial model: needs at least 12 heating hours and 12 idle hours.
messages.Initial observation progress: 12 heating: Initial observation progress: 12 heating hours and 12 idle hours. This is not a reliability rating.
messages.LIVE CONTROL PAUSED · seasonal fallback: LIVE CONTROL PAUSED · seasonal fallback targets
messages.LIVE CONTROL · ThermalPilot controls the: LIVE CONTROL · ThermalPilot controls thermostat targets
messages.Learned parameters and season aggregates: Learned parameters and season aggregates are retained when old observations are compacted.
messages.Learning paused while collection is inac: Learning paused while collection is inactive.
messages.Link rooms heated by one air-to-air pump: Link rooms heated by one air-to-air pump. The zone has one controller and a choice of main-room, average or coldest-room temperature. Any linked room at the shared upper limit pauses zone heating.
messages.Link rooms served by one air-to-air heat: Link rooms served by one air-to-air heat pump. A fireplace can be monitored as an additional heat source.
messages.Live control awaits confirmation. Enable: Live control awaits confirmation. Enable simulation, save, then disable it and confirm to activate thermostat control.
messages.Live control has not been confirmed. Sav: Live control has not been confirmed. Save and confirm to enable real thermostat control.

messages.Modelled cooling: 20°C indoors · −10°C o: Modelled cooling: 20°C indoors · −10°C outdoors · heating off
messages.Negative values reduce estimated heat lo: Negative values reduce estimated heat loss while the fireplace is active; −20% means a 20% reduction.
messages.Negative values temporarily lower the th: Negative values temporarily lower the thermostat target during expensive electricity hours. After a planned heating session, ThermalPilot first restores the room’s normal target. It then chooses reduction only when predicted stored warmth can avoid thermostat heating while supporting room comfort. For example, −1°C allows a 20°C target to be reduced to 19°C during selected costly hours. The reduced target never goes below Minimum allowed temperature. Normal target is restored when reduction is no longer useful; a new planned heating session uses the boosted target. Duration is chosen by the plan, not a fixed number of hours.
messages.No boost planned: normal thermostat dema: No boost planned: normal thermostat demand is sufficient to support the room target.
messages.No continuous next-day price forecast be: No continuous next-day price forecast beyond confirmed prices.
messages.No continuous prices from now: no heatin: No continuous prices from now: no heating plan is available.
messages.No electricity prices are available for: No electricity prices are available for this period. Recorded thermostat activity is shown below.
messages.No observed heating activity: learning i: No observed heating activity: learning is waiting.
messages.No rooms linked. This zone does not cont: No rooms linked. This zone does not control heating.
messages.No usable electricity price list is avai: No usable electricity price list is available.
messages.No weather forecast: current outdoor tem: No weather forecast: current outdoor temperature is held constant.
messages.Not an energy-efficiency or insulation c: Not an energy-efficiency or insulation class.
messages.Notify in Home Assistant when a room tem: Notify in Home Assistant when a room temperature sensor stays unchanged or unavailable for this many hours. A stable room can also have an unchanged reading, so the warning asks you to check the sensor. ThermalPilot sends at most one sensor notification per calendar day. Monitoring runs while ThermalPilot is active; long monitoring gaps restart the timer.
messages.Observation and learning only; no thermo: Observation and learning only; no thermostat control.
messages.Observation only: this heat source does: Observation only: this heat source does not use electricity-price scheduling or thermostat control.
messages.One shared delay starts when the first s: One shared delay starts when the first selected door opens. Heating switches to fan-only after this many seconds while any selected door remains open. The timer resets when all selected doors are closed.
messages.Open a Home Assistant dashboard once, th: Open a Home Assistant dashboard once, then return here to load embedded history cards.
messages.Optional local wind sensor, for example: Optional local wind sensor, for example sensor.netatmo_tuuli_ms using m/s. Valid readings are averaged over the last 30 minutes. ThermalPilot learns a separate wind effect only after enough varied observations; no fixed wind penalty is assumed. Missing, invalid or unchanged-for-two-hours readings are ignored, and normal temperature-based planning and heating continue. Fresh wind correction gradually returns to typical conditions in forecasts further ahead. A stable calm reading may also be ignored conservatively. Units are detected automatically.
messages.Optional price forecast unavailable; pla: Optional price forecast unavailable; planning uses confirmed prices and the normal heat reserve.
messages.Optional sensor with forecast timestamp/: Optional sensor with forecast timestamp/value entries, such as Nordpool Predict FI. Only relative expensive/cheap patterns after confirmed prices are used, so no forecast price unit or additional costs are required. The Source price unit setting applies only to the confirmed total-price sensor. An expensive upcoming period can increase the heat reserve at the end of the known-price plan. Forecast prices are not compared directly with your total prices, used as confirmed prices or used to execute future heating commands. Missing forecasts keep normal planning. Confirmed prices always determine the executable schedule.
messages.Optional wind sensor unavailable or stal: Optional wind sensor unavailable or stale; heating and temperature-based planning continue.
messages.Options are those supported by every sel: Options are those supported by every selected ordinary air-to-air heat pump. Leave unchanged sends no swing command.
messages.Options come from the selected heat pump: Options come from the selected heat pump’s swing_modes. Leave unchanged sends no swing command.
messages.Predicted temperature under the suggeste: Predicted temperature under the suggested plan
messages.Prefer a sensor that includes electricit: Prefer a sensor that includes electricity prices and additional costs, such as VAT, transfer tariffs, electricity tax and retailer margin. A variable electricity-price sensor without these costs also works. If transfer tariffs differ between day and night, including them helps ThermalPilot choose the cheapest heating hours; omitting them can shift heating to hours that are less economical overall. Select a source containing today/tomorrow or timestamped raw_today/raw_tomorrow price lists, and choose the matching source price unit.
messages.Presence sensors lower the fan speed to: Presence sensors lower the fan speed to the selected occupied fan mode for more comfortable use of the garage. Any selected sensor detecting someone activates this mode. Normal heating or standby fan speed resumes when no selected sensor detects presence.
messages.Price forecast available · Extra heat st: Price forecast available · Extra heat storage considered ahead of expensive hours.
messages.Price forecast available · No extra heat: Price forecast available · No extra heat storage needed.

messages.Room response is learned from observed h: Room response is learned from observed heating and cooling, starting with internal estimates.

messages.Select a heat pump in a room or heating: Select a heat pump in a room or heating zone first.
messages.Select the measured supply-water tempera: Select the measured supply-water temperature. A temperature sensor uses its state; a climate entity uses its current_temperature attribute. This is the measured water temperature, not the thermostat’s target. Optional for water-based systems. A valid reading adjusts the estimated heating output. Without it, planning and learning continue from observed thermostat demand, without a water-temperature adjustment. Missing readings do not force fallback targets.
messages.Shared settings apply to ordinary rooms: Shared settings apply to ordinary rooms and heating zones. Garages use their own room settings.
Shared settings apply to ordinary rooms. Garages use their own room settings.
messages.Simulation calculates heating suggestion: Simulation calculates heating suggestions without applying scheduled targets. Disable simulation and confirm to enable real thermostat control. If another automation controls these thermostats, disable it first. Observation and learning continue in both modes.
messages.Simulation is active. ThermalPilot does: Simulation is active. ThermalPilot does not control heating.
messages.Simulation only · scheduled targets are: Simulation only · scheduled targets are not applied
messages.Source checks are available while Therma: Source checks are available while ThermalPilot is active.
messages.Suggested On means the boosted target wi: Suggested On means the boosted target window, including valve timing offsets. Relay On means observed demand; it does not guarantee heat flow.
messages.Summer fallback always applies from 15.5: Summer fallback always applies from 15.5. through 30.9. Outside those dates, it also applies when the day’s lowest forecast temperature is equal to or above this value. For example, a setting of 6°C means the daily minimum must be at least 6°C for ThermalPilot to use summer fallback temperatures. Lower readings already observed that day are included. If a full-day forecast is unavailable outside the summer dates, winter fallback is used.
messages.Summer is 15.5.–30.9., or a complete day: Summer is 15.5.–30.9., or a complete day’s minimum forecast temperature at or above {temperature}°C. Summer fallback uses the shared summer setpoint; winter fallback uses each room’s normal target.
messages.Sunlight through large windows, especial: Sunlight through large windows, especially south-facing windows, can warm a room. No additional physical solar heating system is needed. Select the main direction of those windows to enable solar estimates, or Solar heating off to turn them off. Home Assistant’s location determines seasonal sun elevation and azimuth; cloud conditions come from your weather source. The effect starts at zero and learns gradually. Missing sunlight data assumes no solar warmth; room temperature limits still apply.
messages.Target changes include the shared start/: Target changes include the shared start/stop offsets. The temperature forecast models the planned heating period; actual valve and heat-pump delays must be checked against observations.
messages.Target temperature is outside the allowe: Target temperature is outside the allowed temperature range.
messages.Teal shows the suggested thermostat boos: Teal shows the suggested thermostat boost window; amber shows observed heating demand.
messages.Temperature limit risk: review model ass: Temperature limit risk: review model assumptions and heating capacity.
messages.Temperature limits only preserves the lo: Temperature limits only preserves the lower-to-upper cycle and works without electricity prices. Tariff optimization uses the learned room response and prices to consider earlier heating; the lower limit still takes priority. Missing prices fall back to temperature cycling.
messages.Temperature-only control keeps heating u: Temperature-only control keeps heating until this limit is reached, then uses fan-only. Tariff optimization can heat earlier within these limits.
messages.The cold outdoor endpoint of the initial: The cold outdoor endpoint of the initial heating-hours curve. At this temperature or colder, the starting model assumes the higher daily heating need. Set it below the warm endpoint. Actual room response is learned from observations.
messages.The construction around floor heating, w: The construction around floor heating, which affects how slowly heat is stored and released. Concrete slab describes your heated floor. Choose Not applicable if there is no floor heating. This does not change your configured response lag or erase learned parameters.
messages.The cooling target for this zone. Coolin: The cooling target for this zone. Cooling starts 0.5 °C above this value and stops when any linked room reaches it. This keeps the pump from repeatedly starting and protects colder rooms.
messages.The heat pump’s internal setpoint while: The heat pump’s internal setpoint while heating, separate from the garage sensor’s lower and upper limits. For example, a pump requiring at least 16°C can heat a garage cycling between 5°C and 9°C.
messages.The number is average forecast deviation: The number is average forecast deviation from measured temperature, not an integration fault. Ratings are practical guidance. Color requires at least 20 comparisons. Green also requires beating the no-change benchmark.
messages.The quieter fan speed used when any sele: The quieter fan speed used when any selected presence sensor detects someone in the garage. When no selected sensor detects presence, the normal heating or standby fan speed returns. This changes only fan speed; temperature limits still control heating. Leave unchanged applies no separate occupied fan setting.
messages.The selected heat pump does not report o: The selected heat pump does not report options for this setting.
messages.The selected heat pumps have no common o: The selected heat pumps have no common options for this setting.
messages.The selected period controls past histor: The selected period controls past history. Today and tomorrow are included when prices are published. Recorded activity is shown before now; future suggestions follow the current plan. Price gaps stay empty.

The selected period controls past history. Today and tomorrow are included when prices are published. Recorded activity is shown before now; future suggestions follow the current plan. Price gaps stay empty.
messages.The shortest planned heating session in: The shortest planned heating session in flexible scheduling mode. Longer sessions can be chosen in 15-minute steps. This setting applies to flexible runs; valve opening and closing offsets are applied separately.
messages.The structure below your home: slab on g: The structure below your home: slab on ground, crawl space or basement. A heated concrete floor can be above a basement, so this is separate from Heated floor. Choose Unknown if unsure. This descriptive setting does not reset observation history or learned models.
The swing mode used in fan-only standby. Options must be supported by every selected ordinary air-to-air heat pump. Leave unchanged sends no standby swing command.
messages.The swing mode used while the garage pum: The swing mode used while the garage pump is in fan-only standby. Choose from the selected pump’s supported swing modes. Leave unchanged sends no standby swing command.
messages.The thermostat target used for all confi: The thermostat target used for all configured rooms while ThermalPilot is Passive, if real Active/Passive season setpoint control is enabled. A low summer target normally prevents heating without switching off the thermostats.
messages.The warm outdoor endpoint of the initial: The warm outdoor endpoint of the initial heating-hours curve. At this temperature or warmer, the starting model assumes the lower daily heating need. This curve seeds the model before enough real heating and cooling observations are available.
messages.ThermalPilot applies scheduled thermosta: ThermalPilot applies scheduled thermostat targets while active. Essential data loss returns affected rooms to their seasonal fallback temperature.
messages.ThermalPilot is passive. Planning, colle: ThermalPilot is passive. Planning, collection and learning are stopped.
messages.These forecasts were saved 1, 3 or 6 hou: These forecasts were saved 1, 3 or 6 hours before the measurements. Later readings do not change them. Lower error is better; compare it with simply predicting no temperature change. Different heating, computers and other heat sources can affect the result.
These settings apply to every room.
messages.This measures initial data collection, n: This measures initial data collection, not model trustworthiness. Continue validating forecasts and heating suggestions before enabling live control. Learning continues after initial data collection.
messages.This room belongs to a heating zone. Rem: This room belongs to a heating zone. Removing it also removes its zone membership.
messages.This room is monitored as part of a shar: This room is monitored as part of a shared heating zone. The zone issues one set of commands to its pump.
messages.Time estimate available after at least 2: Time estimate available after at least 24 hours of rate tracking.
messages.Times align to 15-minute boundaries; wid: Times align to 15-minute boundaries; wider views show fewer labels. Hover, focus or tap a price bar or heating period for details.
messages.Times are based on recorded observations: Times are based on recorded observations; gaps are not filled.
messages.Today and tomorrow · past thermostat act: Today and tomorrow · past thermostat activity and future heating suggestions
messages.Upper temperature limit shared by all ro: Upper temperature limit shared by all rooms. Extra heating and heat storage must stay within this limit.
messages.Use the house heating system, or choose: Use the house heating system, or choose a separate air-to-air heat pump. Rooms linked to a heating zone share that zone’s pump; only the zone’s main room issues commands.
messages.Use this room’s own garage limits and ai: Use this room’s own garage limits and air-to-air heat pump controls. House floor-heating limits, heating-water inputs and valve timing do not apply.
messages.Waiting for enough heating and idle obse: Waiting for enough heating and idle observations to estimate the remaining time.
messages.Warn when room temperature readings stay: Warn when room temperature readings stay unchanged or unavailable.
messages.Water-based systems only: lower the ther: Water-based systems only: lower the thermostat target this many minutes before the planned heat-delivery session ends, allowing valves to close. Electric and air distribution ignore this setting and use no closing offset.
messages.Water-based systems only: raise the ther: Water-based systems only: raise the thermostat target this many minutes before the planned heat-delivery session, allowing slow valves to open. Electric and air distribution ignore this setting and use no advance offset.
messages.What produces heat for your house. Selec: What produces heat for your house. Select air-to-water for your water floor system supplied by an air-source heat pump. Gas, oil, wood and district heating need their own fuel-cost logic; choosing a house detail does not yet enable a different controller or reset learned room data.
messages.You have unsaved settings. Discard these: You have unsaved settings. Discard these changes and switch tabs?
messages.Zone rows show recorded heating and cool: Zone rows show recorded heating and cooling only; off and standby periods stay empty. Plan adds suggested heating only for tariff-optimized zones.
messages.Zones are secondary heating or cooling s: Zones are secondary heating or cooling sources. Each room keeps its primary heating system and thermostat.
